# PDF test fixtures (ticket 17)

Deterministically generated PDF samples for the backend PDF text-extraction tests.
Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 tests/fixtures/pdf/generate.py
```

The generator uses only the Python standard library plus the pypdf wheel vendored at
`backend/attachments/pdf/pypdf-6.21.0-py3-none-any.whl` (added to `sys.path` directly,
so no environment install is needed). pypdf's document `/ID` is pinned to a fixed
value, so repeated runs produce byte-identical files and regenerating never shows up
as a spurious diff.

## Expected behaviour

| Fixture | Pages | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text.pdf` | 2 | Page 1 text is exactly `PAGE_ONE_ALPHA`, page 2 exactly `PAGE_TWO_BETA`. Independent per-page literals, so a test can assert that reading page 1 never returns page 2's text. |
| `empty.pdf` | 1 | Valid page with no text. `extract_text()` returns `""`; use for the no-text branch. |
| `encrypted.pdf` | 1 | `is_encrypted` is true and reading without the password raises `FileNotDecryptedError`. With password `fixture-password` it decrypts and page 1 reads `SECRET_PAGE_ALPHA`. |
| `damaged.pdf` | – | Not a valid PDF; opening raises `PdfReadError` (`startxref not found`). |
| `many-pages.pdf` | 501 | Blank pages, all empty text. For page-count limits and per-page read budgets. |
| `partial.pdf` | 2 | Page count is readable as 2 and page 1 extracts `PAGE_ONE_ALPHA`, but reading page 2 raises `PdfReadError` (invalid content stream). Models the partially-parsed case. |

`partial.pdf` is a valid document whose page 2 content-stream bytes are overwritten
in place with invalid operators, at exactly the same length. Keeping the length
identical means the catalog, page tree and xref offsets stay correct — which is the
whole point: structure and page count remain readable while that one page fails.
An earlier approach that pointed page 2's `/Contents` at a non-stream object was
rejected because it silently extracted `""` instead of raising, which would not
exercise the partial-failure path.

Note that opening `encrypted.pdf` with `PdfReader(...)` does not itself raise; the
signal is `reader.is_encrypted`, or `FileNotDecryptedError` when reading pages.

## License

These samples are released into the public domain under
[CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). They are
synthetically generated by `generate.py` from nothing but page text and a base-14
font, so they contain no third-party content.

# PDF vision fixtures (ticket 18)

Deterministically generated samples for the `pdf_render_pages` / vision path.
Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 tests/fixtures/pdf/generate-vision.py
```

Same constraints as the ticket-17 generator: Python standard library plus the vendored
pypdf wheel (`backend/attachments/pdf/pypdf-6.21.0-py3-none-any.whl` added to
`sys.path`, nothing installed), pypdf's document `/ID` pinned to a fixed value, so
repeated runs produce byte-identical files. The scan rasters are not screenshots — they
are built as raw 400×400 RGB bytes in this script and Flate-compressed with `zlib`, so no
external renderer is involved in producing the samples.

Every page is 400×400 pt and every raster is 400×400 px mapped 1:1 onto the page, so
`pdftoppm -scale-to 1600` (what the runtime uses) renders a 1600×1600 image in which one
PDF point is exactly four pixels. That is the scale at which the samples were verified.

## Expected behaviour

| Fixture | Pages | Expected text (`extract_text`) | Expected visual content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scan.pdf` | 1 | `""` — no text layer at all | A three-bar chart: red / green / blue bars standing on a black horizontal axis, page otherwise white. Bar heights are 40 / 80 / 120 pt, so blue is three times as tall as red. |
| `chart.pdf` | 1 | `T18_CHART` plus `10`, `20`, `30` | The same three-bar chart drawn as **vector** rectangles (not an image), with the title `T18_CHART` above and the data labels `10` / `20` / `30` beneath the red / green / blue bars. |
| `mixed.pdf` | 2 | page 1 `MIXED_TEXT_PAGE`, page 2 `MIXED_SCAN_CAPTION` | Page 1 is text only. Page 2 combines the chart raster with real text: the same chart in the upper area and the caption `MIXED_SCAN_CAPTION` below it. |

The three charts share one geometry so a vision answer can be compared across them: bars
80 pt wide at x = 40 / 160 / 280, standing on an axis at y = 40, with heights 40 (red),
80 (green) and 120 (blue). Pure colours — `#ff0000`, `#00ff00`, `#0000ff` — on white, so
bar colour and relative height are unambiguous. `chart.pdf` prints 10 / 20 / 30 as its data
labels; the bar heights are a fixed 4× multiple of those values, which only keeps the pixel
geometry identical to the raster samples.

Human expected visual answers, for asserting a rendered result by eye:

- `scan.pdf`: red, green and blue bars of increasing height, red shortest and blue
  tallest (blue is 3× red), all on a black axis; no text anywhere on the page.
- `chart.pdf`: same bar chart plus the title `T18_CHART`; the labels under the bars read
  `10` (red), `20` (green), `30` (blue), i.e. the tallest bar carries the largest value.
- `mixed.pdf`: page 1 shows only `MIXED_TEXT_PAGE`. Page 2 shows the bar chart with
  `MIXED_SCAN_CAPTION` printed underneath it — a page that has both a real text layer and
  visual content, which is the case where reading text alone would be misleading.

## Regenerating and verifying

```bash
python3 tests/fixtures/pdf/generate-vision.py                 # write the three samples
sha256sum tests/fixtures/pdf/{scan,chart,mixed}.pdf          # stable across runs
pdftoppm -scale-to 1600 -png tests/fixtures/pdf/scan.pdf /tmp/scan   # visual check
```

Note that the ticket-17 samples above attach their font as an indirect *stream* object,
which poppler rejects ("font resource is not a dictionary") — their text extracts but
renders as nothing. The generator for these samples writes the font as a plain dictionary
so the text is actually visible in a render; the ticket-17 generator is left untouched.

Like the ticket-17 samples, these are synthetic and released into the public domain under
[CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/): they contain only
solid rectangles, a raster built from solid rectangles, and base-14 Helvetica text.
